title: Cristin Hubbard Reflects on a Career Spent Bringing Innovation to Patients – and Why Working at BioMarin Has Her More Energized Than Ever
summary: Learn how the Chief Commercial Officer's professional journey has shaped her and prepared her to lead at BioMarin.
body_markdown:
Cristin Hubbard is still motivated by the same idea that sparked her earliest interest in healthcare and eventually led her to biopharma: getting medicines to the people who need them most.


At BioMarin, Cristin says she feels the impact of that commitment as strongly as ever.


“What I love about working in rare disease is the connection to the communities we serve,” says Cristin, BioMarin’s Chief Commercial Officer. “You feel like every contribution matters so deeply for patients and their families.”


From early work as a medicinal chemist to leading global commercial teams, her career has been shaped by a consistent focus on bringing innovation closer to patients. She’s applying those experiences to help BioMarin leverage its global footprint and capabilities and ultimately reach more people living with rare genetic conditions around the world.


We sat down with Cristin to reflect on her professional journey, her leadership philosophy and why she feels like her work at BioMarin is the most impactful of her career.


## **Q: When you describe your career journey, what are some of the key inflection points that stand out?**


I always knew I wanted to be in healthcare. My mom was a nurse, and that had a big influence on me from a young age. I initially thought I’d go into patient care directly, but in college I shifted toward science and ended up working as a medicinal chemist at a small biotech.


I loved the work – it felt like solving a massive puzzle with the potential to become a medicine one day. But over time, I realized I wanted to be closer to getting medicine to patients. Drug discovery is profoundly important work, but is at the very beginning of the process, and I was drawn to work further downstream in the pharmaceutical life cycle – clinical development, portfolio planning, product strategy, commercialization, getting treatments to healthcare providers and patients.


That realization led me to business school and into roles that moved progressively closer to patients, first in portfolio and product strategy, and then into commercial leadership. At first, I thought, “There’s no way – a scientist becoming a commercial leader?” But I took the leap when the opportunity came, and it was one of the most formative experiences of my career.


Looking back, I was fortunate to get exposure across the entire value chain. At the time, it didn’t feel like a straight line, but each step added another tool to my proverbial belt.
